summary.7-10: Jesus tells a storm to be quiet.
summary.11-14: The disciples are terrified, and Jesus is asleep.
summary.15-18: A nature miracle that is really a question about identity.

7-10: Jesus and his friends got into a boat to cross the lake. Jesus was so tired he fell asleep.
A big storm came. Water started filling the boat and his friends were frightened. They woke him up.
Jesus stood up and said to the wind and the waves, “Quiet! Be still!” And everything went calm.
11-14: It was evening, and Jesus asked to cross to the other side. He had been teaching all day and fell asleep on a cushion in the back of the boat.

A squall came down — the lake is famous for them — and the boat began to swamp. Several of these men were professional fishermen, and they were frightened, which tells you how bad it was. They woke him with a question that is really an accusation: don't you care?

Jesus spoke to the storm as if it were a person: 'Quiet! Be still!' It stopped. Then he asked them why they were afraid, and they became more frightened than they had been in the storm, asking each other who this actually was.
15-18: Mark stages the scene to end on a question, not on a rescue: 'Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?' The miracle serves the christology.

In the Hebrew Bible, authority over the sea belongs to God alone — Psalm 107 has sailors crying out in a storm and the Lord stilling it to a whisper, in almost the same sequence. Mark's readers would have heard the echo.

The disciples' fear increases after the storm stops, which is exactly right. A storm is dangerous; a man who speaks to storms and is obeyed is a category problem. Mark's whole gospel presses that problem until someone answers it correctly at the cross.

whatHappened.7-10: Jesus told the storm to stop, and it stopped.
whatHappened.11-14: Jesus calmed a storm with a word, and his friends were left asking who he really was.
whatHappened.15-18: Jesus stills the sea with a command, and Mark uses the moment to raise the question of his identity.

whatItTeaches.7-10: Jesus is stronger than the things that frighten us.
whatItTeaches.11-14: Jesus being asleep did not mean he did not care. It meant he was not panicking about what was panicking them.
whatItTeaches.15-18: Mark's point is not primarily comfort but identity: the one who commands the sea is doing something Scripture reserves for God.

thinkAboutIt.7-10: What makes you frightened? What would you like to say to Jesus about it?
thinkAboutIt.11-14: The disciples asked 'don't you care?'. Have you ever wanted to ask God that?
thinkAboutIt.15-18: Why might Mark end the episode with a bigger fear than the one it began with?

pray.7-10: Jesus, when I am scared, help me remember you are with me.
pray.11-14: Jesus, you were not panicking when they were. Help me trust you when things feel out of control.
pray.15-18: Jesus, you commanded the sea and left them asking who you were. Give me an answer I actually live by.

prompt.7-10: What did Jesus say to the storm?
prompt.11-14: What did Jesus do about the storm?
prompt.15-18: How does Mark end the episode?

explain.7-10: He told the wind and waves to be quiet, and they were.
explain.11-14: He rebuked the wind and told the sea to be still — and it obeyed him.
explain.15-18: With the disciples' question: 'Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?'
